report.title: Concurrent-session races on the shared git index and file leases
report.question_or_target: When two sessions or agents operate on the same working tree, does a broad staging operation sweep another agent's files, and do the advisory file leases actually prevent the overlap?
report.headline_answer: Linux remeasure preserved the finding. Each broad shared-index staging operation exposed the sibling file in git diff --cached, and Agent A staged Agent B bytes for the overlapping path. coordination.leases granted an exclusive lease then allowed the second identity direct write; a consulted second acquire returned CONFLICT and did not grant. No process listens on 127.0.0.1:8812, so the deployed service remains NOT-CHECKED as a write gate.
named_probes_verbatim: Probe 1: run two agents against one scratch tree with overlapping file sets and inspect what each staging operation captured, using git diff --cached as the oracle.

Probe 2 (mechanically different): lease-level test - acquire a lease from one identity and attempt the conflicting write from another, recording whether the write is blocked, warned, or silently allowed; an advisory lease that nothing consults is documentation, not a control.

targets.target: A broad staging operation on a shared index sweeps the sibling session's files.
targets.answer: Agent A captured agent-b.txt and Agent B captured agent-a.txt; both git diff --cached snapshots contained agent-a.txt, agent-b.txt, and shared.txt.

targets.target: Overlapping file writes can cause one session to stage the other writer's bytes.
targets.answer: Agent A intended shared.txt but its staged shared.txt began writer=agent-b.

targets.target: The pinned upstream exclusive file lease prevents a conflicting direct write.
targets.answer: BlueLake acquired an exclusive lease. GreenCastle wrote leased.txt with exit 0, empty stdout/stderr, and replaced the bytes. A consulted second acquire returned CONFLICT (granted=false). The lease API does not mediate the filesystem write.

targets.target: The currently deployed lease service prevents the same overlap.
targets.answer: No service listened on 127.0.0.1:8812, so no deployed-version claim is made.

targets.target: Shared-tree concurrency is protected against cross-agent staging and write overlap.
targets.answer: Shared-index broad stage and overlapping last-writer are CONFIRMED; pinned exclusive lease is REFUTED as a write gate; deployed 8812 service is NOT-CHECKED.
